summary_html: An intake **screen** is elevated to a formal **investigation/assessment** under state criteria. CAPTA and CFSR establish the federal expectations for screening, timelines, and investigative quality.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — screening/investigation conditions for funding  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review framework

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Affirming termination, the Court set out the ex parte petition, preliminary hearing and probable-cause hearing sequence under § 40-11-7.1 and held that the twelve-month period for termination may run from the child's placement in DCYF care rather than from a formal finding of abuse or neglect.
key_cases.relevance: It explains the statutory escalation from DCYF's ex parte filing to preliminary and probable-cause hearings.
key_cases.quote: Next, a hearing on the petition must be held within seven days.

key_cases.holding: Abuse and neglect findings were affirmed on medical evidence of fourteen non-accidental fractures, and the mother's Fourteenth Amendment challenge to DCYF's seventy-two-hour hold was not preserved because the parents waived the Rule 15(c)(5) probable-cause hearing.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms that a seventy-two-hour hold escalates into a judicial proceeding at which the parent must act to preserve objections.
key_cases.quote: Therefore, we conclude that Kimberly's challenge to the temporary hold on the children was not preserved for appeal.

key_cases.case_name: Hatch v. Department for Children, Youth & Their Families
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Constitution permits a Rhode Island DCYF caseworker to take temporary custody of a child without a hearing when the caseworker has a reasonable suspicion that abuse has occurred or is imminent, and the DCYF worker here met that standard, so qualified immunity barred the claim.
key_cases.relevance: Hatch rejects any requirement that DCYF complete a full investigation and reach probable cause before escalating to custody.
key_cases.quote: It follows, therefore, that a parent's right to the care, custody, and control of a minor child is inviolate unless a case worker has such a suspicion.

key_cases.holding: The abuse and neglect decree against the mother was vacated because the evidence did not clearly and convincingly show that she inflicted or allowed the infant's injuries, where she reported the bruising immediately and followed medical advice.
key_cases.relevance: It shows an intake escalating to an eleven-day abuse and neglect trial on medical evidence alone.
key_cases.quote: We are of the opinion, therefore, that Anna's response to discovering the bruising, even if arguably dilatory, does not support a finding of abuse or neglect.

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3(a)
Physicians, certified registered nurse practitioners, and other healthcare providers — additional immediate oral and written report duty, R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-6
reporting_details: In Rhode Island any person who has reasonable cause to know or suspect that a child has been abused or neglected must transfer that information to DCYF within 24 hours (R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3(a)).

other: Other abuse or neglect including any action or lack of action which results in harm or potential harm to the physical, mental health, behavioral health or welfare of the child and which is not covered by the other allegations

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately upon receipt of the report
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3

timeline_requirements.deadline: 30 days, with an extension of up to 15 additional days on supervisor or administrator approval
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in 214-RICR-20-00-1 § 1.9(F), which states that "all efforts are made" to complete each investigation within 30 days
